get.description:
Returns the chart of accounts for the organization tied to the API credentials.
Use optional filters (for example updated.gt) to sync only accounts changed since a prior run.

post.description:
Adds an account to the chart of accounts for the organization.
The account currency is inherited from the organization, its status is ACTIVE, and its default grouping and closing behavior are derived from the selected type and subtype.

Initializes the entire chart of accounts for a bare organization in one atomic call.
The organization must have no existing chart of accounts; otherwise the request fails with 409.
The complete request is validated before any accounts or groups are created; validation failures return 400 without leaving a partial chart of accounts.

Structural invariants match CSV import: exactly one `Accounts Receivable`, `Accounts Payable`, `Sales Tax Liability`, and `Retained Earnings`;
at least one `Unbilled Revenue`, `Prepaid Expense`, and `Deferred Revenue`.
The same default group scaffold as CSV import is created.
Each account's optional `parent_grouping` reuses a scaffold group by name or creates a nested group under the account type root.
When the request contains exactly one `Prepaid Expense` account, expense accounts may omit `prepaid_account_code` to default to it;
when it contains multiple `Prepaid Expense` accounts, each expense account must reference one by code.
`Cash in Transit` is auto-created and must not appear in the request.

get.description:

Each subsidiary includes its ID, currency, and timezone. Use its ID with endpoints that require `subsidiary_id`.
Legal entity subsidiaries also include `legal_name`, `address` and `tax_id`, as shown in Settings → Subsidiary Details.

When the hierarchy feature and hierarchy API support are both enabled for your organization:

- Each subsidiary includes `parent_subsidiary_id`: its direct parent's ID, or `null` if it has no parent.
- The response includes `root_subsidiary_id`: the ID of the configured hierarchy root.
  The root can differ from the default subsidiary.

Otherwise, both fields are omitted.
Parent and root IDs are included even if you cannot access those subsidiaries.
The root ID is included even when the list is empty.
Use a token with access to all subsidiaries to read the complete hierarchy.

Legal entity subsidiaries also include `legal_name`, `address` and `tax_id`, as shown in Settings → Subsidiary Details.

When the hierarchy feature and hierarchy API support are both enabled for your organization,
the response includes `parent_subsidiary_id`. This is the direct parent's ID, or `null` if there is no parent.
The parent ID is included even if you cannot access the parent.
If either feature is disabled, `parent_subsidiary_id` is omitted.

Returns one approval workflow: the conditions that decide which entries it applies to, and the ordered
layers of approvers that must sign off. This is the control definition, not a record of approvals given.
Approval workflows are not versioned — the response describes the workflow as it stands now, and an
update overwrites it in place.

configure are rejected too (see the individual fields).

Entries already awaiting approval are unaffected, because an entry copies the layers it needs when
approval starts; only entries registered after this call use the new definition. Deadlines and layer
escalation rules are not part of this contract and are cleared, exactly as saving a workflow in
Rillet clears them.

post.summary: Preview the invoice schedule for a contract

The FULL scope is used when contract invoices are generated and sent directly from Rillet. In this case, Rillet automatically assigns the invoice numbers.

The REVENUE_RECOGNITION_ONLY scope is intended for situations where contracts and invoices are issued from another system and only need to be recorded in Rillet for accounting purposes. In this workflow, users must provide the invoice numbers manually. Other fields can be populated based on the data imported from the external system.

For example, if your organization issues invoices through an external billing platform but tracks financials in Rillet, you should select REVENUE_RECOGNITION_ONLY. If Rillet handles the entire invoicing and sending process, choose the FULL scope.

omitted from the request body is cleared. To set or clear individual keys without
disturbing the rest, use patch-contract-metadata instead. Null, empty, and
whitespace-only values clear a single key. Archived keys may only be cleared, never changed.
Every key must name a definition assigned to contracts: an unknown key, or one assigned

ignored. The write is atomic: if any key fails validation, nothing is written.

null, empty, or whitespace-only value to clear it. Prefer this over

keys you did not name. Archived keys may only be cleared, never changed. Every key must
name a definition assigned to contracts: an unknown key, or one assigned only to another
entity type, fails the request with a 400. Keys are never silently ignored. The write is
atomic: if any key fails validation, nothing is written.

parameters.name: contract_id
parameters.description: UUID of the contract to patch metadata for.

Returns draft contracts with cursor pagination. Draft contracts are staged records that appear in the Rillet UI under

parameters.name: customer_id

post.description:
Stages a contract in the "draft" holding state instead of creating it directly as an active contract.
Draft contracts appear in the Rillet UI under "Draft" for a human to approve or reject.

## Deduplication

**To prevent duplicate draft contracts on retry, supply at least one `external_references` entry with a
stable `(type, id)` pair.** When you POST again with any matching `(type, id)` pair, the prior draft record
is replaced with the new payload.

Draft contracts created without any `external_references` are not deduplicated — every POST creates a new
record.

## External reference types

Each reference's `type` must match a slug already defined under Rillet Settings → External References for
the organization; unknown slugs return a 400. References attached at create time are preserved when the
draft contract is promoted to an active contract.

## Promotion

Promotion to an active contract happens through the Rillet UI. The public API does not currently expose a
programmatic promotion endpoint.

post.description:
A matching creation approval workflow returns HTTP 202 with invoice_id, approval_request_id, and status PENDING.
This is a proposal, not a created invoice. Retrieve its contents using retrieve-an-invoice-creation-proposal.
For approval proposals, pass idempotency_key on the initial call and retain it across retries.
The key is optional; each call without one creates a new submission, including retries.
The key does not deduplicate legacy creation when approvals are disabled or the invoice belongs to a contract.
A rejected proposal remains closed; a deliberate new invoice uses a new key.

Rillet supports two invoice scope types: FULL and REVENUE_RECOGNITION_ONLY. The selected scope determines how the invoice is created and what information the user needs to provide.

The FULL scope is used when the invoice is generated and sent directly from Rillet. In this case, Rillet automatically assigns the invoice number.

The REVENUE_RECOGNITION_ONLY scope is intended for situations where the invoice is issued from another system and only needs to be recorded in Rillet for accounting purposes. In this workflow, users must provide the invoice number manually. Other fields can be populated based on the data imported from the external system.

For example, if your organization issues invoices through an external billing platform but tracks financials in Rillet, you should select REVENUE_RECOGNITION_ONLY. If Rillet handles the entire invoicing and sending process, choose the FULL scope.

parameters.name: idempotency_key
parameters.description: Stable key for retries of an approval proposal. Ignored when approvals are disabled or the invoice belongs to a contract. Use a new key for a distinct proposal.

post.summary: Uploads a document to a manual journal entry
post.description:
Appends one PDF, JPEG, PNG, or XLSX of at most 20 MiB to an existing manual journal entry.
Create the journal entry first; for asynchronous imports, wait until the entry is available.
Existing attachments are preserved. Repeating an upload creates another attachment.
A journal entry can have at most 10 attachments, including files uploaded through the Rillet application.
Attachments may be added to approved entries and entries in closed periods without changing accounting data or approval status.
System-generated and non-posting entries are not supported.

System-generated and non-posting entries are not supported.

post.summary: Matches bank transactions to existing records
post.description:
Matches bank transactions to existing records. You can include different record types in one request, subject to
the supported match combinations. To book a difference, provide reconciliation_adjustment.account_id.
Optional reconciliation_adjustment.fields are custom field and value IDs applied to the adjustment entry,
not to the matched records. Rillet calculates the difference.

post.summary: Matches bank transactions with new quick entries
post.description:
Creates a separate quick entry for each bank transaction in transaction_ids, using the same requested details.
The transactions are not combined into one many-to-one (N:1) match. With line_items, supply exactly one ID.

post.summary: Matches two bank transactions as a transfer
post.description:
Matches two bank transactions as a transfer. The source transaction may be incoming or outgoing; the
transaction amounts determine the direction. Cross-subsidiary transfers require access to both subsidiaries. 
For a same-subsidiary transfer with a difference, provide reconciliation_adjustment.account_id;
reconciliation_adjustment.fields apply to the adjustment line. If either bank transaction has a fee, provide 
fees_account_id to book it. A transfer with fees on both bank transactions is not supported.

get.description:
Returns the month-end close checklist for one accounting month: every task with its notes, due date,
preparer, reviewer queue, completion and sign-off state. Use it to report close progress or to find the
task_id needed by update, complete and sign-off. Resolve preparer and reviewer user ids to people with
list-members (match on user_id). Responds with HTTP 404 when no checklist exists for the month.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return tasks in this status.

parameters.name: preparer_ids
parameters.description: Only return tasks whose assigned preparer, or the user who completed them, is one of these user ids (comma-separated). A task completed by someone other than its assigned preparer matches either user.

parameters.name: reviewer_ids
parameters.description: Only return tasks where one of these user ids is a reviewer (comma-separated).

patch.description:
Partial update of one task's details and assignments. Fields omitted from the body are left unchanged.
Completion and reviewer sign-offs cannot be set or cleared here; use complete-a-close-checklist-task and
sign-off-a-close-checklist-task. A reviewer who has already signed off keeps their place in the queue:
a reviewer_ids list that drops or moves them is rejected with HTTP 409. Every preparer and reviewer must
be an active member of the organization (see list-members). Returns the updated task.

post.description:
Marks the task as prepared, recorded as completed by the connected user at the current time. Requires
an OAuth connection made by a named user; API keys are rejected with HTTP 403 because they do not act as
a user. A task that is already completed is rejected with HTTP 409 so an earlier preparer's record is
never overwritten. Returns the updated task.

post.summary: Signs off a close checklist task as reviewer
post.description:
Records the connected user's review sign-off on a completed task. Requires an OAuth connection made by a
named user; API keys are rejected with HTTP 403. The task must be completed first (HTTP 409 otherwise).
Only a reviewer on the task who has not signed off yet may sign off (HTTP 403 otherwise); when the
organization enforces an ordered reviewer queue, it must also be their turn. A fully signed-off task is
rejected with HTTP 409. Returns the updated task.

post.summary: Reports API or MCP bugs and missing features
post.description:
Found something surprising, confusing, or missing while using the API or MCP tools? Tell us, even if you found a workaround.
Report unclear tool schemas, confusing results, missing filters, excessive pagination, or missing bulk operations.
Send one observation per request. Describe what you were trying to do and what you expected; for bugs, also include
what actually happened. For MCP feedback, set endpoint to /mcp and include the affected tool name in description,
for example list_all_journal_entries. You do not need to know the tool's underlying REST path.
For API feedback, set endpoint to the affected API path. A writable API key or OAuth token with write scope is required.
The organization and submitting credential are recorded from authentication, so you do not need to provide them.

Creates a `type` for use in `external_references`. If the organization already has a type with this
`slug`, it is returned unchanged with `200`; otherwise it is created and returned with `201`. Reserved
names are rejected.

ApprovalWorkflow.description:
An approval workflow: the conditions deciding which entries it applies to, and the ordered layers of
approvers that must sign off.

active.description:
Only active workflows are evaluated. Read-only here: a workflow is activated and deactivated in
Rillet, so this value can change without a definition update.

priority.description:
Evaluation order among the active workflows of the same type, ascending and zero-based — the first
workflow whose conditions match is the one applied, and later ones are skipped. Assigned by the
server: a workflow is put last when created, and again when reactivated. Not necessarily unique;
ties are resolved by `id`.

approval_layers.description:
Layers of approvers in ascending `order`, each one actionable only once the previous is satisfied.
The entry is approved when every layer is satisfied. At most five.

methods.description:
How approvers are asked to act. `IN_APP` is the only method Rillet acts on today; `EMAIL` and
`SLACK` can appear on workflows configured before they were withdrawn, and no notification is
delivered for them.

submission_sources.description:
Entry points governed by this workflow. Null or an empty list means manual entry in Rillet only.
An explicit list applies exactly to those sources. Provider import, scheduled sync, and reimport
are the runtime sources represented as Connected integrations in Rillet.

updated_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC timezone (must end with 'Z'). Covers activation and reordering as well as
definition changes.

ApprovalWorkflowRequest.description:
An approval workflow's definition, as sent when creating or replacing one. A workflow's `type` never
changes, and `active` changes only through activation in Rillet, so an update must send both back
unchanged.

type.description:
Required, and must equal the workflow's current type — a workflow cannot be moved between types,
because `priority` orders workflows within one type. Contract and Invoice workflows are not
supported by this endpoint.

active.description:
Required, and must equal the workflow's current value — activation is a dedicated operation in
Rillet, so a definition update never changes it. Read the workflow first if you are unsure.

methods.description:
Only `["IN_APP"]` is accepted today: `EMAIL` and `SLACK` deliver nothing, so they are rejected
rather than stored.

submission_sources.description:
Optional source scope for Bill, Charge, Charge Reversal, and Reimbursement workflows. Omit this
field or send null to preserve the stored scope. An empty list means manual entry in Rillet only;
a non-empty list applies exactly to the listed sources. To select Connected integrations, include
`PROVIDER_IMPORT`, `SCHEDULED_SYNC`, and `REIMPORT`.

ApprovalWorkflowType.description:
The kind of record a workflow applies to. Contract and Invoice are retained for backward-compatible
reads but cannot be updated through this endpoint.

ApprovalWorkflowSubmissionSource.description:
Runtime entry point for an approval-governed expense. `INTERNAL_API` and `SAMPLE_DATA` are
system-managed and can appear in responses but cannot be added through this API.

ApprovalWorkflowConfigurableSubmissionSo.description:
Customer-configurable entry point for an expense workflow. Connected integrations are represented by
`PROVIDER_IMPORT`, `SCHEDULED_SYNC`, and `REIMPORT` together.

ApprovalWorkflowConditionLogic.description: How the workflow's conditions combine: `AND` requires every condition to match, `OR` any of them.

ApprovalWorkflowMethod.description:
How approvers are asked to act. Only `IN_APP` is acted on; `EMAIL` and `SLACK` were withdrawn and
deliver nothing.

ApprovalWorkflowSourceType.description:
Whether a journal entry was created by a person (`MANUAL`) or by Rillet from another record such as a
bill, invoice or amortisation schedule (`SYSTEM`). `ALL` matches either.

ApprovalWorkflowCollectionOperator.description:
How a condition compares against a set of values: `ANY_OF` matches when at least one of them applies,
`NONE_OF` when none does.

ApprovalWorkflowConditionGroup.description:
A set of conditions combined by one logical operator, together with any nested groups, which combine
into it the same way. A group carries at least one condition or one nested group. Today a workflow
always has a single group with no nested groups; `groups` exists so that combinations such as
`A AND (B OR C)` can be expressed without reshaping this contract.

conditions.description:
Conditions in this group, exactly as stored. A workflow carries at most five conditions across the
whole tree, not five per group.

A journal-entry workflow with no `SOURCE_TYPE` condition applies to manually created entries only,
whatever its other conditions say: that restriction is implied rather than stored. Add a
`SOURCE_TYPE` condition to have a workflow apply to entries Rillet generates from bills, invoices
or amortisation schedules.

groups.description:
Nested groups, each combined into this one by `logic`. Nesting is at most three levels deep.
Always empty today.

RevenuePattern.description: DAILY divides revenue equally per day. EVEN_PERIOD divides revenue equally per calendar month. PROGRESS uses a progress plan; the supported measure MILESTONES recognizes allocated revenue on milestone completion and requires a one-time price. FULL contract creation supports an explicit progress plan or snapshots the referenced product's template. Existing non-progress behavior is unchanged.

MilestoneValueMode.description: Values are non-negative plain decimal strings with no exponent notation. PERCENTAGE supports at most 4 decimal places; AMOUNT supports at most 10 decimal places. Excess decimal places, including trailing zeros, are rejected rather than rounded. PERCENTAGE values are whole percentages ("30" means 30%), range from 0 to 100, and must total exactly 100. AMOUNT values on product templates are proportional weights in the product's currency and must total more than zero; they are not fixed contract obligations.

MilestoneExpectedOffset.description: Forecast offset from the contract line start date, not an invoicing or recognition trigger. Uses a non-negative integer count and a single calendar unit. Zero offsets are returned as {"count": 0, "unit": "DAYS"}.

key.description: Stable integration identifier, unique within the plan ignoring case. Keys that parse as UUIDs are not allowed.

name.description: Display name, unique within the plan ignoring case and repeated whitespace.

sequence.description: Ordering within the plan. Each milestone must have a distinct positive JSON integer sequence; fractional numbers and strings are rejected.

value.description: A non-negative plain decimal string with at most 4 decimal places in PERCENTAGE mode or 10 decimal places in AMOUNT mode, including trailing zeros. Excess decimal places are rejected rather than rounded. In PERCENTAGE mode, "30" means 30%; values must be at most 100 and sum to exactly 100. In AMOUNT mode, values are proportional weights whose total must be positive, not fixed contract amounts.

expected_offset.description: Optional forecast offset from the contract line start date. Omit or send null for no offset.

id.description: Server-generated milestone identifier.

address.description: Deprecated: use billing_addresses. In responses, the first address in billing_addresses. In requests without billing_addresses, it creates or edits that first billing address in place; the customer's other billing addresses are left untouched.

billing_addresses.description: All of the customer's billing addresses, returned in a stable order; the first is the default for new contracts and invoices. On update the list is authoritative: addresses sent with an id are updated, addresses without an id are added, and stored addresses left out are removed. Removing an address that is used by a contract or an invoice that can still be edited is rejected with a 400 naming those documents. Omit to leave billing addresses unchanged; send an empty list to remove them all. Cannot be combined with address.

shipping_addresses.description: All of the customer's shipping addresses. Same rules as billing_addresses. Cannot be combined with shipping_address.

emails.description: All of the customer's emails. On update, send the full list: emails with an id are kept or edited, emails without an id are added, and emails left out are removed (omitting emails, or sending an empty list, removes them all). A removed email is also removed from every contract email_selection; to change an email and keep it selected, send its id. Rejected: an id on create, an id that doesn't belong to this customer, the same id twice, or the same address and type twice (addresses are compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces).

send_invoices_automatically.description: When set to true, invoices for this customer will be automatically sent via email on the invoice date.

send_payment_reminders.description: When set to true, an email will be sent to customers periodically if they have not paid an invoice.

allow_online_payments.description: Allows this customer to pay invoices online via Stripe, and must be true before auto-payment can be set up for them. Omit on create to leave online payments off; omit on update to keep the customer's current setting. Enabling it requires Stripe to be configured for at least one subsidiary.

tax_ids.description: The customer's tax IDs. Omit on create for no tax IDs. On update, omit to keep the current tax IDs, send an empty list to clear them, or send a list to replace them all. Adding or changing tax IDs requires the customer to have an address, and they are validated with the organization's tax provider when one is connected.
